Items.Authors: Tania Sofia Gomes Machado, Federico Battaini, Simone Di Filippo, Alessandro Ballone, Kalyan K. R. Santhakumari, Elisa Portaluri, Demetrio Magrin, Davide Greggio, Davide Giughello, Dhiraj Gupta, Andrea Bianco, Michele Frangiamore, Marco Dima, Oleksandra Rebrysh, Maria Bergomi, Carmelo Arcidiacono, Luca Marafatto, Valentina Viotto, Roberto Ragazzoni, Jacopo Farinato, Pierre Jouve, Felipe Pedreros Bustos
Items.Title: A comparative study of strategies to replicate sodium LGS in a laboratory environment
Items.Abstract: The next generation of Adaptive Optics (AO) systems relies heavily on Laser Guide Stars (LGS) to expand sky coverage. Since LGS are extended objects, unlike Natural Guide Stars (NGS), dedicated AO technologies are required. Accurate testing of these new technologies on benches like MATTO and the Ingot WFS (I-WFS) requires high-fidelity laboratory replication of LGS properties, including variable profiles and geometry. We present a comparison of four distinct LGS-like source solutions tested on the I-WFS Bench: screens (OLED/LED), fluorescent materials (Rhodamine/Eosin Y), Spatial Light Modulators (SLMs) and holograms. By using the pupil uniformity of the I-WFS as a performance metric, we evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of each method to guide future laboratory test bench development.

Items.Authors: Christian M. Pommranz, Emanuele Perinati, Michael J. Freyberg, Chris Tenzer, Andrea Santangelo
Items.Title: A digital twin of the eROSITA camera: readout modeling workflow for Monte Carlo simulations
Items.Abstract: As SRG/eROSITA is the first X-ray instrument at L2, the characterization of its instrumental background is of special importance. Previously, Geant4 simulations of the filter wheel closed background were conducted using a highly detailed mass model of the eROSITA camera. In this work, a readout modeling workflow was developed for post-processing of the Geant4 simulation results. This new workflow precisely models the entire readout procedure and produces FITS files that are compatible with the eROSITA Science Analysis Software System (eSASS), resulting in a digital twin of the eROSITA camera. This workflow has been shown to reproduce the drop at high energies above 9 keV observed in the measured filter wheel closed spectrum. Additionally, the workflow provides new insights by complementing the results of the previous Geant4 simulations with additional observables. Furthermore, the new workflow enables the use of identical data analysis for simulation and measurement data.

Items.Authors: Stephen J. C. Yates, Auke Veninga, Geert Keizer, Willem Jellema, Martin Eggens, Nick de Keijzer, Shahab O. Dabironezare, Jochem J. A. Baselmans, Lorenza Ferrari
Items.Title: A flexible full system far infra-red kinetic inductance detector test facility
Items.Abstract: We have developed an ultra-low background cryogenic test facility to support the future missions like PRIMA (satellite) and POEMM (balloon), enabling us to push the (detector) technological readiness. The system is equipped with cryogenic re-imaging optics and is initially designed to operate in either a 3-4 THz or 6-12 THz band, by choice of quasioptical filters. The unique property of the system is that it has two operation modes. The first allows direct wideband access to the lab environment with a power loading of ~25 fW/pixel, enabled with cryogenic Neural-Density filters of ~50dB attenuation. Alternatively, the cryostat window can be closed and a cryogenic blackbody placed in the pupil stop at 4K, which allows for absolute calibration at ultra-low loading. Using this system enables us to present the first beam patterns and spectral response of lens-coupled absorber KID arrays at 6-12 THz, with a good match to simulations.

Items.Authors: Jiahao Zhou, Wenfei Liu, Yingfu Wang, Mengmeng Qian, Haoyang Zhang, Xianke Song, Kai Yun, Hongzhuan Hu, Jianping Wang, Jiaru Chu, Ping Zhang, Zhigang Liu, Zengxiang Zhou
Items.Title: A Grid-Based Matching Algorithm for Back-Illuminated Spots Using the Distribution Pattern of Fiber Positioning Units on LAMOST
Items.Abstract: To achieve efficient closed-loop control of the 4,000 fiber positioning units in the LAMOST telescope, this work addresses the limitations of the conventional nearest-neighbor matching method in handling dense and occasionally anomalous fiber positions. We propose a novel gridded spot matching algorithm, which utilizes the inherent regularity of the fiber layout as prior knowledge. By constraining the matching search within localized grid cells, the algorithm transforms a global matching challenge into efficient local comparisons. Implementation in LAMOST's closed-loop system shows that this method significantly improves both the processing speed and the robustness of fiber position detection.

Items.Authors: Zhen Zhang, Guifeng Chen, Yonggang Gu, Chao Zhai
Items.Title: A high-speed 3D measurement method for fiber-array end faces based on fringe projection
Items.Abstract: The surface accuracy of fiber arrays significantly impacts the efficiency of spectroscopic telescopes. Measuring fiber endfaces clamped in miniature ceramic sleeves is extremely challenging due to their small size and reflectivity. We propose a binocular 3D measurement method based on fringe projection: multiple fringe patterns are projected to obtain the unwrapped phase of each fiber, and its 3D coordinates are reconstructed. The RANSAC algorithm fits an optimal sphere, and the distribution accuracy is evaluated using the distance of each fiber to this sphere. Prototype laboratory experiments demonstrate that this method can accurately measure fiber endface positions and evaluate array surface accuracy.

Items.Authors: Chelsea Adelman, Steph Sallum
Items.Title: A JWST kernel phase interferometry search for post main sequence planets
Items.Abstract: Most exoplanets orbit stars that will eventually become white dwarfs (WDs), yet knowledge of their post-main-sequence (post-MS) evolution is still unconstrained. While some post-MS exoplanets have been detected, a large sample of directly-imaged systems is needed to constrain their evolution mechanisms. The faintness of WDs, which prohibits adaptive optics correction for most targets, makes space-based imaging an attractive approach. However, detections on orbits where migrating post-MS exoplanets may reside remain technically challenging. Kernel phase interferometry (KPI) can access these separations by treating a conventional telescope as an interferometer in post-processing. This yields moderate contrast (well suited to detecting cold giant planets around faint WD hosts) within the diffraction limit. We present a KPI analysis of JWST imaging of a large sample of WDs. We constrain the occurrence rate of WD-orbiting planets and discuss the implications for post-MS exoplanet evolution.

Items.Authors: Ulf Seemann, Christian Fruck, Alexander Buron
Items.Title: A mid-IR Fabry-Perot Etalon calibrator for VLT/CRIRES+
Items.Abstract: We present a concept study for a novel Fabry-Perot Etalon (FP) calibration system covering the mid-IR range 2um - 5um (KLM bands) of ESO's high-resolution infrared spectrograph CRIRES+ at the VLT. The FP system is optimized to provide robust wavelength calibration in the KLM bands and means to calibrate the spectrograph's entrance slit curvature independent of nighttime and telescope time on sky, thereby enhancing the CRIRES+ calibration capabilities out to 5um. We derive the system requirements, discuss the challenges and feasibility associated in this wavelength regime, present a concept design and its implementation into CRIRES+, and evaluate the achievable performance.

Items.Authors: Adrián Calzadilla González, Nicolás Adrián Rodríguez-Linares, Luz Maria Montoya Martínez, Noelia Feijóo Amoedo, Yolanda Martín Hernando
Items.Title: A modular drag-and-drop GUI for SAOS using an MVVM architecture
Items.Abstract: A new graphical user interface (GUI) is presented for the Solar Adaptive Optics Simulator SAOS. Current AO simulation pipelines typically require direct coding, limiting accessibility and slowing prototyping. The GUI allows users to configure complete adaptive optics systems without programming, using drag-and-drop components for atmospheric modules, deformable mirrors, Shack-Hartmann sensors, and scientific cameras. It also provides interactive visualization of wavefront maps, surface deformation profiles, and performance metrics. The system follows a modular MVVM architecture, improving scalability and ease of extension, and integrates seamlessly with SAOS through a data-abstraction layer. Use cases and preliminary results demonstrate usability for engineers, researchers, and students. Future work includes multi-user support, cloud execution, and machine-learning-based adaptive control.

Items.Authors: Lanqiang Zhang, Qianhan Zhou, Nanfei Yan, Shuai Zhang, Jinsheng Yang, Changhui Rao
Items.Title: A monolithic upgrade of the NVST adaptive optics system for multi-mode and prominence observations
Items.Abstract: The adaptive optics (AO) system of the 1-m New Vacuum Solar Telescope has been comprehensively upgraded to improve system stability and to enable closed-loop AO correction for solar prominences. The previous AO system integrated AO, GLAO, and MCAO modes but suffered from a complex optical layout and thermal instability in the Coude room, leading to alignment sensitivity and performance degradation. To address these limitations and meet the requirements of prominence correction, the system has been completely redesigned into a compact, monolithic, single-platform configuration. A reconfigurable composite wavefront sensor supports AO, GLAO, and MCAO modes, while a dedicated chromospheric wavefront sensor enables closed-loop AO correction on solar prominences. This presentation focuses on the optical and opto-mechanical redesign of the system and its expected performance improvements. Commissioning is scheduled for May 2026, and initial high-resolution observations will be presented.

Items.Authors: Zhemin Cai, Jonathan Moller, Christopher Coote, Jessica R. Zheng, Helen M. McGregor, Michael Goodwin, Jonathon S. Lawrence, Rémi Giroud, Florence Laurent, Alexandre Jeanneau, Johan Richard
Items.Title: A multi-physics thermal-mechanical framework for BlueMUSE: IFU layout evaluation and thermal-enclosure performance assessment
Items.Abstract: BlueMUSE is a blue-optimised, medium-resolution panoramic integral-field spectrograph under development for the VLT, now fully entering the design phase. With transmission down to 350 nm, R ≈ 3500, and a 1 arcmin² field of view, it will support a wide range of galactic science.    To ensure optical stability during night-time observations, we developed a multi-physics framework combining finite-element analysis and computational fluid dynamics to quantify allowable temperature variations on key optical elements. Three IFU-layout configurations were assessed, and the preferred design was selected based on thermal sensitivity, mechanical robustness, and manufacturability. Thermal boundary conditions from the full-telescope model were mapped onto a high-fidelity instrument model, enabling detailed prediction of temperature evolution across critical optics. The resulting variations remain within limits, confirming that the proposed enclosure concept provides adequate stability.

Items.Authors: Nicolas J. Flagey, Laurent Pueyo, Laura E. Coyle, Marcio Melendez, Randal Telfer, Tyler M. McCracken, Matt Lallo, Rémi Soummer, Leonid Pogorelyuk, Iva Laginja
Items.Title: A semi-analytical error budget for the Habitable Worlds Observatory
Items.Abstract: In this paper we present a suite of representative top-level error budgets for the Habitable Worlds Observatory produced by the ULTRA-CT team. This error budget relates the contrast stability (key to exoplanet detection using differential imaging) to the wavefront variance at the entrance of the coronagraph instrument, integrated over a suite of past temporal scales.

Items.Authors: Xue Yang, Chen Zhang, Zhixing Ling, Yuan Liu, Weimin Yuan
Items.Title: A significant micrometeoroid impact damage event on the EP-WXT in September 2025
Items.Abstract: The Einsten Probe (EP) satellite has been in operaion for two years, during which time the Wide-field X-ray Telescope (WXT) on board has been experiencing micrometeoroid impact almost every month. In September 2025, one such events resulted in the simultaneous capture of impact traces by multiple detectors. This paper provides a detailed report on the pixel damage caused by this event, including a comprehensive overview of the time of occurrence, the distribution of detector position, the duration of impact, the extent of the damage, and the observed changes.

Items.Authors: Roser Juanola-Parramon, Christopher Stark, Amber Young, Paul Scowen
Items.Title: A standalone near-UV coronagraph for detecting atmospheric biosignatures with the Habitable Worlds Observatory
Items.Abstract: The near-ultraviolet (NUV) band enables detection of key atmospheric species such as O₂ and O₃ through their strong absorption between 200–400 nm. To access these features, the Habitable Worlds Observatory would require a standalone NUV coronagraph. Although NUV coronagraphy is challenging, its role as a characterization instrument relaxes several design trades: the inner working angle need only match that of the visible coronagraph, and prior knowledge of planet locations allows non-circular dark zones that improve throughput.    We present a preliminary design for a dedicated NUV coronagraph informed by science requirements, expected exoplanet yields, and atmospheric retrieval needs. We outline the rationale for separating the NUV instrument from the main coronagraph, evaluate candidate coronagraph architectures, assess polarization aberrations, and discuss suitable UV detectors and wavefront-control approaches.

Items.Authors: Rosa Calvi
Items.Title: A unified Python tool for ESO-compliant data products: from Astro-WISE (VST) to MUSE
Items.Abstract: Ensuring that processed data products meet ESO header and metadata standards is essential for seamless ingestion into the ESO Science Archive. As part of VSTCen operations, I developed a lightweight Python tool that automatically corrects, validates, and completes FITS headers for VST data reduced in Astro-WISE. The tool has been generalized and successfully adapted to MUSE, by implementing instrument-specific keyword rules. This flexible framework reduces manual intervention, improves data-flow reliability, and accelerates public data releases. Although currently implemented for VST and MUSE, the tool can be easily adapted to other instruments, offering a robust and reusable solution to the broader community for generating archive-ready data across heterogeneous surveys.

Items.Authors: Arika Egan, Richard Cartwright, Joseph Linden
Items.Title: A visible IFU for HWO: characterizing ocean world habitability inside and outside of the solar system
Items.Abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO), NASA’s next Astrophysics Flagship mission, will absolutely revolutionize astrophysics, and has the potential to conduct complementary planetary science. A prime opportunity to understand exo-ocean worlds and their habitability can be found in visible-wavelength spatially resolved spectroscopy of solar system bodies. In the case of Europa, there are several absorption and emission features spanning the optical bandpass that offer unprecedented insight into the moon’s surface features, plume activity, and exosphere. HWO's long operational lifespan enables long-term monitoring of transient phenomena like geyser eruptions and surface composition changes. Such observations will provide breakthrough progression toward understanding the extent of interior-surface material exchange, which is essential for determining if they harbor habitable environments. To this end, we present a preliminary visible wavelength integral field spectrograph for HWO.

Items.Authors: Giulia Conenna, Willem Jan Vreeling, Daniela Perez Capelo, Dimitry Lamers, David Thoen, Martijn Veen, Jochem J. A. Baselmans, Lorenza Ferrari
Items.Title: Accelerated aging tests of kinetic inductance detectors for the PRIMA Mission
Items.Abstract: We present the results of an accelerated aging study performed on absorber coupled Kinetic Inductance Detectors (KIDs) developed for the PRIMAger instrument on the PRIMA mission. PRIMAger uses single-polarized leaky-lens antenna-coupled KIDs for the PRIMA Polarimetric Imager (PPI), and lens-absorber-coupled KIDs for the PRIMA Hyperspectral Imager (PHI). These devices are based on NbTiN resonators with an aluminum section for radiation absorption, while PPI integrates a 100 nm SiN membrane coupled to the aluminum coplanar waveguide. In this study we focused specifically on the absorber KIDs for PHI, as they use the thinnest aluminum film (22 nm).  Because aluminum thin films are sensitive to environmental exposure and can undergo surface oxidation that may affect performance, it is essential to evaluate their long-term stability. The aim of these tests is to assess the stability of the devices under environmental stressors experienced during production, transport, pre-launch and launch.

Items.Authors: Yutong Qiao, Chit-Ho Hui, Renbin Yan, Ruoyu Zhou, Sabyasachi Chattopadhyay, Michael P. Smith
Items.Title: Accurate testing of multi-mode optical fibers and surprises from octagonal-core fibers
Items.Abstract: Octagonal-core fibers show great potential in astronomical spectroscopy instruments due to their excellent scrambling performance, which ensures a stable line spread function (LSF). However, such high scrambling performance could be accompanied by pronounced focal ratio degradation (FRD), which can significantly compromise instrument efficiency. In this study, to precisely measure FRD and characterize the scrambling performance, the fiber test stand was upgraded with an enlarged aperture and a carefully optimized optical layout. The upgraded system supports faster input focal ratios, provides an improved diffraction limit, and enables higher-accuracy focal ratio measurements through a new alignment procedure that achieves a highly telecentric input beam. Our experimental results confirm the superior scrambling performance of octagonal-core fibers. Moreover, these fibers exhibit negligible FRD when coupled with an F/2.8 input beam, which is ideal for sky surveys.

Items.Authors: Germain Garreau, Thomas Birbacher, Adrian M. Glauser, Jonah T. Hansen, Julio Pino, Eckhart Spalding, Sascha P. Quanz
Items.Title: Achieving efficient broadband spatial filtering for the Nulling Interferometry Cryogenic Experiment (NICE): status and plan
Items.Abstract: The Nulling Interferometry Cryogenic Experiment (NICE) is a laboratory testbed intended to explore the feasibility of deep ( 90%) is challenging to achieve over such a large bandwidth.  The current test bench operating at ambient temperatures is equipped with quantum-cascade lasers (QCLs) at 4.0 and 4.7µm wavelengths. We present the different options explored in the test bench for spatial filtering. We test a single-mode hollow-core fiber and compare its coupling efficiency and null performance with an InF3 fiber. We also explore the combination of phase-induced amplitude apodization (PIAA) with single-mode fibers and its expected performance and error budget.

Items.Authors: Javier León Gil, Marta Belío Asin, Nicolás Adrián Rodríguez Linares, Miguel Núñez Cagigal, Mary Barreto, José Manuel González Cava, Juan Albino Méndez Pérez
Items.Title: Active optics control in the European Solar Telescope (EST)
Items.Abstract: The European Solar Telescope (EST), a 4-m class solar telescope with an integrated Multi-Conjugate Adaptive Optics system, will operate in an open-dome configuration, exposing the entire structure to wind and challenging image stability. This study focuses on the role of Active Optics (AcO), responsible for real-time corrections using selected compensators: M1 and M2 for deformation and misalignment correction, and M3 and M6 for pupil alignment. The AcO system mitigates low-frequency distortions caused by gravity, thermal effects, and quasi-static wind loads. The paper examines the system’s key components, including actuators, sensors, and operational scenarios, and evaluates different control strategies and algorithms to enhance performance and robustness. As the telescope remains in its design phase, all analyses rely on simulation results. Finally, the study outlines the proposed control strategy and planned actuation ranges for the AcO.

Items.Authors: Chloe Miossec, Iain Steele, Helen Jermak, Stuart Bates, Richard Ashley
Items.Title: Adapting a Shack‑Hartmann wavefront-sensor with a built‑in calibration source for the New Robotic Telescope
Items.Abstract: We present an updated Shack–Hartmann wavefront sensor designed to assist segment alignment for the New Robotic Telescope (NRT), a 4‑metre, fully autonomous facility whose primary mirror is assembled from 18 hexagonal 1-metre segments. Following tests in the laboratory, a first prototype has been built and successfully tested on the Liverpool Telescope (LT) as a proof-of-concept. Following difficulties experienced in the analysis process, a second‑generation design now incorporates an integrated artificial light source to simplify calibration and accelerate alignment procedures. The sensor incorporates a lenslet array to image the telescope pupil and map each mirror segment to dedicated subapertures, enabling direct measurement of piston and tip and tilt for individual segments. The instrument is optimised for robotic operation: it is robust, compact, and economical, relying mainly on off‑the‑shelf components.

Items.Authors: Pablo Gutierrez Cheetham, Pablo Alberto Fuerte Rodriguez, Antonio Ramon Manescau Hernandez, Frédéric Derie
Items.Title: Advanced calibration unit electronics for VLT fors-upgrade
Items.Abstract: FORS1 was one of the first instruments installed at the VLT, yet still in high demand. An upgrade is underway, carried out by ESO and the Astronomical Observatory of Trieste (INAF), to bring it back soon with new, advanced features.  One key feature is the ability to perform instrument calibrations at any time (day or night) without constraining telescope activities. This is achieved by projecting the calibration light internally rather than toward the back of the M3 of the VLT.  This new design features advanced electronics to control and monitor the calibration lamps (Pencil, Arc, and Halogen), incorporating specialized Beckhoff power-monitoring terminals, for voltage and current, as well as small embedded I²C bus sensors for light intensity, operating time, and temperature that can be deployed near the lamps. Also introducing a compact shutter to block the light while keeping the lamps turned on, and a Kniel EtherCAT controlled power supply.  The presentation focuses on the electronics

Items.Authors: MAHSHID SHIRI, Enrico Cascone, Christian Eredia, Pietro schipani
Items.Title: Advanced motion control of Stewart platforms: integrating Kane's method with nonlinear model predictive control
Items.Abstract: This paper presents a control methodology for high-precision motion control of a Stewart Platform-a key component for positioning systems. The approach merges Kane's Method for minimal dynamic modeling with a Nonlinear Model Predictive Controller (NMPC). The NMPC optimizes actuator forces in real-time while explicitly enforcing physical and singularity avoidance constraints. The integrated framework implemented in MATLAB/Simulink shows superior trajectory tracking accuracy and dynamic robustness, which provides an essential solution to the extreme pointing stability required by MORFEO at the ELT.

Items.Authors: Benjamin M. Cromey, Laura E. Coyle, Tyler M. McCracken, Jeremy Shugrue, Joseph Ho, Thomas Peters, Sebastian Valencia, Dominic Maes, Dustin Putnam, Daniel A. Porpora
Items.Title: Advancing critical technologies and integrated modeling for HWO in year 8 of the ULTRA program
Items.Abstract: The Ultrastable Large Telescopes Research and Analysis (ULTRA) program led by BAE Systems Space & Mission Systems continues to press forward with technology advances and system level insights for NASA’s Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO). The team continues its dual focus on 1) high-fidelity simulation leveraging models provided by NASA to evaluate their capabilities and risks as potential architectures and 2) hardware demonstrations/studies to address high priority technology gaps in stable mirrors, precision thermal control, and ultrastable sensing and actuation. This presentation will summarize recent achievements by this team and how they support the technology and concept maturation of HWO.

Items.Authors: Brianna Peck, Jessica R. Lu, Lianqi Wang, Brooke DiGia, Richard Dekany, Antonin H. Bouchez, Peter L. Wizinowich, Maxwell A. Millar-Blanchaer, Mark R. Chun, Philip Hinz, Charles-Antoine Claveau
Items.Title: Advancing Keck visible-light adaptive optics: optimizing trade studies for KOLA
Items.Abstract: We present ongoing development of visible-light adaptive optics simulations for the Keck I telescope as part of the proposed Keck Optical Laser guide star Adaptive optics (KOLA) system. By modeling how multiple deformable mirrors and laser guide stars work together, we explore design choices that will help KOLA deliver sharp, high-resolution images across a wide field of view. These studies support the continued development of next-generation adaptive optics capabilities at Keck.

Items.Authors: Shannon M. Duff, Jason E. Austermann, Kyuyoung Bae, Johannes Hubmayr, Gregory Jaehnig, Michael J. Link, Tammy J. Lucas, Christopher Rooney, Corwin Shiu, Joel Ullom
Items.Title: Advancing TES bolometer performance for next-generation CMB instruments
Items.Abstract: The feedhorn-coupled planar-orthomode-transducer (OMT)-fed transition-edge sensor (TES) bolometer has been demonstrated in large-format arrays for multiple successful Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) polarimetry experiments spanning frequencies from 20-300 GHz. We report on a set of test pixel measurements aimed to advance the detector performance for the next generation CMB instrument through better understanding of the efficiency of each mm-wave component in the circuit. Additional development of a calibration TES based on the superconducting proximity effect to set its properties will lead to increased dynamic range for in-lab optical loading. We will present details of the design, fabrication, and characterization of these test pixels.

Items.Authors: Sofia Fatigoni
Items.Title: Aliased noise characterization in BICEP Array 150GHz time-division multiplexed detectors
Items.Abstract: We analyze the performance of the BICEP Array 150 GHz TES detectors with a focus on noise behavior. Early observations showed excess noise from the TDM readout, where high-frequency fluctuations are aliased into the 0.1–1 Hz science band. We trace this excess to elevated TES loop gain, driven by a steep α, which speeds detector response but amplifies out-of-band noise that is then aliased. Using 400 kHz open-loop noise spectra, we identify this high-frequency excess and compute its expected aliased contribution. We show that reducing loop gain, by operating the focal plane at slightly higher temperature or by increasing the multiplexing rate, effectively mitigates the noise. NET tests confirm that running ~100 mK above nominal improves stability and reduces NET by ~10–15%. These results highlight the link between TES parameters, noise performance, and overall sensitivity for next-generation CMB polarimeters.

Items.Authors: Gizay Yolalan, Derya Öztürk Çetni, Bülent Güçsav, Ebru Uzunçam, Onur Şatır, Elif Köksal, Cahit Yeşilyaprak
Items.Title: Alignment and performance evaluation of the k-mirror field stabilization system of the DAG400 telescope
Items.Abstract: Large-aperture mirrors require alt-azimuth telescope mountings due to their mass, and in such systems, optical field correctors are essential to ensure the invariance of scientific data. The DAG400 telescope features a novel design in which the optical field-correcting system is positioned inside the telescope flange rather than on an external optical bench, distinguishing it from other telescopes worldwide.  The K-mirror system of the DAG400 consists of three flat mirrors coated on Zerodur substrates. Currently undergoing on-sky testing, this system possesses twelve degrees of freedom. This study presents in detail the alignment procedure used to match both the mechanical and optical axes of the K-mirror with the main telescope axis. The final performance of the system is also evaluated based on the latest observations.

Items.Authors: Lorenzo Zago, Laurent Jolissaint
Items.Title: An advanced active optics actuator for primary mirrors exposed to dynamic wind loading
Items.Abstract: The paper presents progress and updated results for a novel type of axial actuator for active optics systems of primary mirrors aimed at telescopes operated in open air.   The current prototype is designed as a force feedback actuator with a typical maximum force of 500 N, a resolution better than 0.1 N, which are typical performances for current active optics axial actuators.  The novel aspect is a fast dynamic response with a closed loop bandwidth approaching 10 Hz, hence able to compensate wind gust buffeting in open air and dynamic loads of any origin.

Items.Authors: Joshua Fitzpatrick, Christopher Mendillo
Items.Title: Analysis of atmospheric wavefront distortions from PICTURE, a balloon-based optical telescope
Items.Abstract: PICTURE-D is a NASA balloon mission intended to directly image debris disks in nearby star systems. The observatory floats at altitudes up to 40km, above 99% of Earth’s atmosphere. This greatly reduces the effects of atmospheric turbulence and seeing, allowing for much more stable stellar wavefronts. To counteract turbulence, most modern optical telescopes utilize various adaptive optics (AO) systems. Many AO systems observe the incoming signal with wavefront sensors and aim to correct the effects of atmospheric distortion in near real-time with deformable mirrors. Although greatly reduced by altitude, PICTURE-D must still contend with these distortions as well as effects from thermal and mechanical deformations and imperfections in optical components. During three flights in 2019, 2022 and 2025, the mission has collected a vast amount of wavefront sensor data, detailing exactly what errors were present and at what times. We present an analysis of the wavefront distortions and attempt

Items.Authors: Christoph Baranec, Reed L. Riddle, Yuhei Takagi, James E. Lyke, Christophe S. Clergeon
Items.Title: Analysis of laser-satellite deconfliction for astronomical observatories
Items.Abstract: We present an analysis of laser-satellite deconfliction across four astronomical laser observatories, using Program Approval Messages (PAMs) for fixed azimuth and elevation ranges. This study uses new visualization tools to evaluate the operational efficiency of laser keep-out-cone half-angles from the standard 2.5 degrees down to the 0.1-degree minimum. We further assess how different science exposure durations impact the total percentage of available open-time during observing nights. Finally, we analyze historical trends in PAM data to quantify the growing impact of satellite mega-constellations and the efficacy of specific waiver protocols on ground-based laser astronomy.

Items.Authors: Fabio Tenegi Sanginés, Roberto Simoes, Óscar Tubío Araújo
Items.Title: Analytical, FEMs, and experimental study of natural frequencies of subsystems of the laser guide star for GTC
Items.Abstract: The LGS Facility (LGSF) for GTC generates an artificial star (Laser Guide Star or LGS) in the high atmosphere to help the GTCAO system correct for atmospheric turbulence. The LGSF's core is a high-power laser operating at the Na D2 line (589 nm). This beam is expanded and routed by the Laser Transfer System (LTS) to the Laser Launch Telescope (LLT), which points and launches it into the sky. The light stimulates sodium (Na) atoms in the mesosphere, causing them to emit photons and thus creating the LGS.  The aim of this talk is to present both analytical and finite element studies, as well as experimental results regarding the eigenfrequencies of some of the main subsystems of the GTCAO LGS system.

Items.Authors: Marco Landoni, ANDES Consortium
Items.Title: ANDES, the high resolution spectrograph for the ELT: the software ecosystem toward the Preliminary Design Review
Items.Abstract: In this paper, we present an overview of the software architecture designed for the ArmazoNes high Dispersion Echelle Spectrograph (ANDES), developed in preparation for the instrument Preliminary Design Review (PDR). First, we provide an in-depth description of the control software, outlining how it has been conceived to ensure reliable operation of a complex, highly distributed instrument such as ANDES.   In this context, we discuss the integration of the ELT Instrument Control Framework, highlighting the architectural choices that proved essential for meeting the stringent technical and operational requirements of the project. Second, we describe the suite of science-oriented software tools that will accompany ANDES and support its use by scientist. These include the Exposure Time Calculator, the Observation Preparation tools, and the Data Reduction Library functionalities that are crucial for efficient planning and for the systematic processing of raw data produced by the instrument

Items.Authors: Fabio Rossi, Enrico Pinna, Guido Agapito, Nicolò Azzaroli, Cédric Plantet, Giulia Carlà, Ben Buky, Cedric Taissir Heritier
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrograph for the ELT: updates from the prototyping work package of the SCAO module
Items.Abstract: The ANDES SCAO module for the ELT spectrograph is undergoing prototyping to validate key components and algorithms. Simulation work assessed two piston-sensing concepts for the reference path: a double-wavelength LIFT sensor (modeled in SPECULA) and a photonic-lantern–based approach (analyzed using a GPU-optimized waveguides simulator). In parallel, the SPRINT algorithm, designed to track Pyramidal Wavefront Sensor (PyWFS) misregistration, was developed and successfully validated on-sky at the Large Binocular Telescope. The experimental results demonstrated SPRINT's robustness for real-time control, guiding its integration into the SCAO architecture. These activities collectively advance the technical readiness and inform crucial design decisions for the ANDES SCAO module.

Items.Authors: Menghao Wang, Chao Zhai
Items.Title: Anti-collision detection system based on precise feedback control in LAMOST
Items.Abstract: LAMOST(Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopy Telescope) is an Extremely Large Active Reflective Schmidt Telescope located in Hebei, China. In the past few years we are working on a new generation LAMOST fiber position system. The new system has more fibers, totally different communication system, and a newly designed feedback control system. With this new system, we are able to solve a problem haunting us for years, that is the collision between fiber control units. Collision can cause severe damage to fiber control units, but there was little we can do to solve it. In the new system, we designed a precise real-time close-loop feedback control system. With this system, not only can we detect fibers' real-time position, but we can also make rapid precise responses. This paper mainly introduces the precise feedback control system, and the anti-collision strategies.

Items.Authors: Joseph R. Eimer, Robert H. Barkhouser, Stephen A. Smee, Rolf Chini, Marek Górski, Gergely Hajdu, Albert J. Harding, Stephen C. Hope, Paulina Karczmarek, Weronika Narloch, Grzegorz Pietrzyński, Piotr Wielgórski
Items.Title: Araucaria InfrRed Imager (AIRI) instrument design
Items.Abstract: The Araucaria InfraRed Imager (AIRI) is a new instrument designed to provide high-precision near-infrared photometry in the J, H, and Ks bands on the 2.5-m telescope at the Cerro Murphy Observatory in Chile. AIRI will enable sub-percent geometric distance measurements to eclipsing binary systems in the Milky Way and Magellanic Clouds, providing substantially improved constraints on the extragalactic distance scale and, consequently, on the Hubble constant. AIRI builds on the WHIRC camera developed for the WIYN telescope, incorporating updated cryogenic cooling, an H2RG detector array, and targeted modifications to the original optical prescription to optimize performance for the new telescope. This paper presents the AIRI instrument design, including the optical layout, opto-mechanical architecture, and control-system framework. The system is designed to deliver diffraction-limited performance across the

Items.Authors: Thomas L.R. Brien, Mayank Baghoria, Chris Benson, Peter S. Barry, Marcial Becerril-Tapia, Simon Doyle, Chris J. Dunscombe, Harry Gordon-Moys, Sam Rowe
Items.Title: Array-scale performance of polarisation-sensitive kinetic inductance detectors for sub-95 GHz applications
Items.Abstract: KIDs have become one of the dominant detector technologies in the far-infrared and mm-wave domains for numerous astrophysical fields. Thin-film aluminium presents a fundamental low-frequency limit to their response for KIDs made with this material of approximately 95 GHz. This limit excludes such detectors from fully exploiting 90 GHz band which is commonly studied in cosmology. We present the array-scale performance of KIDs fabricated from a composite material of aluminium and titanium to produce a transition temperature within the range 0.90-1.05 K. We present characterisation of single arrays consisting of approximately 400 KIDs fabricated on a single 100-mm silicon wafer and readout. We examine the performance of these arrays considering fundamental sensitivity, polarisation response, and on the wafer scale due to fabrication factors. We describe the packaging of the wafer and how vibrational noise is minimised. Finally, we show early results from scaling this to the 150-mm wafers

Items.Authors: Germain Garreau, Denis Defrère, Romain Laugier, Peter M. Chingaipe, Marc-Antoine Martinod, Thomas Mattheussen, Kwinten Missiaen, Johan Morren, Gert Raskin, Muhammad Salman, Wannes Verstraeten, Azzurra Bigioli, Simon Gross, Michael Ireland, András P. Joó, Lucas Labadie, Stephen Madden, Alexandra Mazzoli, György Medgyesi, Ahmed Sanny, Bart Vandenbussche
Items.Title: Asgard/NOTT: cryogenic characterization of the mid-infrared photonic chip
Items.Abstract: Asgard/NOTT is the first long-baseline nulling interferometer that will be operational in the southern hemisphere. It is an L’-band (3.5-4µm) instrument optimized to characterize hot exozodiacal dust and young giant planets orbiting around the snowline of nearby main-sequence stars. NOTT uses a photonic beam combiner made of Gallium Lanthanum Sulfide (GLS), manufactured at Macquarie University and characterized at ambient temperatures at Universität zu Köln. Using the test bench of the NOTT instrument assembled at KU Leuven, and its test cryostat, we successfully cooled the chip down to ~140K and performed its first cryogenic characterization. The results show that the GLS photonic chip behaves as expected at cryogenic temperatures. We investigate an anti-reflection coating to reduce its Fresnel losses and increase its throughput to ~50%, and we test the coating’s resistance at cryogenic temperature

Items.Authors: John C. Wilson, Randolph P. Hammond, Robert Barkhouser, Stephen A. Smee, Nancy J. Chanover, Miranda van Iersel, Brooklyn K. McLaughlin, Noah S. Measells
Items.Title: ASPEN fore-optics preliminary design
Items.Abstract: We present the preliminary design of the fore-optics for the ARC SPectrograph for Echelle iNvestigations (ASPEN), a new optical echelle slit spectrograph for the Astrophysical Research Consortium (ARC) 3.5-m Telescope at Apache Point Observatory in New Mexico.  ASPEN will feature high throughput, particularly in the blue, with simultaneous wavelength coverage of 340 -- 1000 nm wavelength range.  Based on slit choice, the spectrograph will have user-selectable resolutions from 32,000 to 64,000.  The fore-optics include an Atmospheric Dispersion Corrector (ADC), retractable calibration feed module, tip-tilt stabilization module, retractable iodine cell, and slit viewer. The ADC and tip-tilt system are integral parts of our goal of maximizing overall throughput. We review the optical and opto-mechanical design of each module and discuss the rationale for our design choices.  We also discuss prototypes of a two-slice image slicer module that will be located in the slit mechanism.

Items.Authors: Fulvio Gianotti, Ismam Abu, Marcello Lodi, Alessandro Tacchini, Giuseppe Malaspina, Marco De Benedetto, Federico Fiordoliva, Marco Costi, Giordano Mancini, Daniele Gregori, Mirco Pinetti, Massimo Sardo, Matteo Rosi, Davide Obbi, Pietro Bruno, Andrea Bulgarelli, Luca Castaldini, Vito Conforti, Mattia Corpora, Alessandro Costa, Valentina Fioretti, Valentina Giordano, Andrea Giuliani, Stefano Gallozzi, Christine Grivel, Federico Incardona, Nicola La Palombara, Giuseppe Leto, Fabrizio Lucarelli, Andrea Mandica, Emilio Mastriani, Kevin Munari, Giovanni Pareschi, Nicolò Parmiggiani, Valerio Pastore, Federico Russo, Pierluca Sangiorgi, Salvatore Scuderi, Sebastiano Spinello, Gino Tosti
Items.Title: ASTRI Mini-Array On-Site ICT Infrastructure for High-Availability and Efficient SCADA Operations
Items.Abstract: The ASTRI Mini-Array is an array of nine dual-mirror Cherenkov telescopes installed at the Teide Observatory, where seven telescopes are already deployed and two are acquiring Cherenkov data. Its operations rely on a dedicated on-site ICT infrastructure designed to support control, data acquisition, monitoring, and timing distribution. The system integrates a virtualized environment for telescope control, high-throughput bare-metal acquisition coupled with BeeGFS storage, Kubernetes-based services for monitoring and data quality assessment, and a White Rabbit timing network ensuring nanosecond synchronization. The infrastructure is now fully operational and has been extensively used by the AIV/T and SCADA teams during commissioning, providing critical feedback for optimization and validating its reliability for long-term scientific operations.

Items.Authors: Maxwell Service, Avinash Surendran, Jacob Taylor, Antonin Bouchez, Percy Gomez, Mahawa Cisse, Charlotte E. Guthery
Items.Title: Automated performance optimization for operations at W.M. Keck Observatory
Items.Abstract: The current operational approach to optimization for the Keck adaptive optics systems requires substantial manual intervention. For example, an operator needs to open a separate tool which analyzes recent telemetry and estimates the ideal gain. This approach is poorly suited to maintaining good performance as conditions or guide star parameters change, which means we can realize performance gains by automating this process. It is also important that automated optimization be stable as it needs to run with no supervision for entire AO nights without harming the performance of the system. Work has been done to automate this process to no longer require user intervention, starting with automatic loop gain optimization for the high order and tip tilt loops. This paper describes the methods used and the resulting operational improvements.

Items.Authors: Boon-Kok Tan
Items.Title: Band-splitting diplexing-hybrid for dual-band simultaneous-observing sideband-separating heterodyne mixers
Items.Abstract: Superconductor-insulator-superconductor (SIS) receivers are vital for black-hole imaging with the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT), which uses a global mm/sub-mm array to form an Earth-sized interferometer. Future EHT expansions demand simultaneous multi-band capability to capture rapid variability near the event horizon, support multi-line spectroscopy, and enable phase-transfer calibration from lower to higher frequencies. Although space missions use free-space diplexers for multi-band operation, their loss at ambient temperature makes them unsuitable for high-sensitivity ground-based systems. A prior cryogenic design by Masui et al. (PASJ 2021) showed that multi-band partitioning is feasible using three cascaded waveguide diplexers. Building on this, we introduce a new architecture that provides simultaneous dual-band, continuously tunable RF coverage with sideband separating operation in both bands, requiring only one set of quadrature hybrids and filters.

Items.Authors: Erik Sundin, Leif Helldner, Magnus Strandberg, Igor Lapkin, Mathias Fredrixon, Sven-Erik Ferm, Denis Meledin, François Joint, Alexey Pavolotsky, Victor Belitsky, Vincent Desmaris, Rolf Ahlman
Items.Title: Beam Characterization System for Cartridge‑Type Cryogenic THz Receivers
Items.Abstract: The Group for Advanced Receiver Development (GARD) designs components and receiver front ends for millimetre wave and terahertz radio astronomy observatories. To ensure optimal performance, both components and receiver systems must be characterized under cryogenic conditions using various measurement techniques. A critical aspect of this process is the investigation of receiver optics, which ensures precise alignment and maximum sensitivity. We present a refurbished and redesigned beam measurement system, upgraded with improved hardware to enhance accuracy and reliability. The system supports measurements in the 275–373 GHz range and is adaptable to other frequency bands. To automate routines, a dedicated graphical user interface (GUI) has been developed, built upon the GARD Measurement System (GMS), a hardware abstraction layer enabling communication with instruments and data acquisition. At the conference, we will present the updated design, the GUI software, and obtained results.

Items.Authors: Drew M. Miles, Jake A. McCoy, Fabien Grise, Ross McCurdy
Items.Title: Blazed UV grating development for the Habitable Worlds Observatory and beyond
Items.Abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) and other future missions require advancements in component technologies to achieve their science objectives. We discuss here several techniques developed through Strategic Astrophysics Technologies programs to manufacture blazed gratings for ultraviolet (UV) spectroscopy. Prototype gratings fabricated with electron-beam lithography (EBL) and KOH etching have shown peak-order groove efficiencies in excess of 65% across the far and extreme UV. While efforts continue to further optimize EBL and KOH-etch processes for UV applications, development has begun on two additional fabrication techniques to produce blazed UV gratings: EBL paired with ion-beam etching, and thermally activated selective topography equilibration. We provide an overview of each fabrication technique, review recent performance measurements, and discuss the path toward developing blazed UV gratings for HWO and beyond.

Items.Authors: Christopher Coote, Jessica R. Zheng, Jonathon S. Lawrence, Zhemin Cai, Jonathan Moller, Helen McGregor, Florence Laurent, Alexandre Jeanneau, Rémi Giroud, Johan Richard
Items.Title: BlueMUSE splitting and relay optics: design strategies for a sixteen-channel blue-optimised IFU spectrograph
Items.Abstract: BlueMUSE is a blue-optimised, medium spectral resolution, panoramic integral field spectrograph under development for the Very Large Telescope (VLT). The project is now entering design phase. With an optimised transmission down to 350nm, spectral resolution of R~3500 on average across the wavelength range, and a large FoV (1 arcmin2), BlueMUSE will open up a new range of galactic and extragalactic science cases facilitated by its specific capabilities.    Centrally in the beam path, the splitting and relay optics divide the field into sixteen channels and form intermediate images for the integral field units. This contribution presents the preliminary optical design strategy and mechanical proposals, using air-spaced crystalline-glass achromat pairs to deliver the required optical performance, stability and channel clearance. We introduce opto-mechanical concepts for high-precision, athermal mounting methods in the context of the BlueMUSE instrument.

Items.Authors: Daniel Bodenmüller, Philipp Huke, Kalaga Madhav, Martin M. Roth
Items.Title: BluePOCO: a tunable visible frequency comb from microring resonators for astronomical spectrographs
Items.Abstract: Frequency combs have emerged as powerful tools for high-precision wavelength calibration in astronomical spectroscopy, enabling unprecedented accuracy and long-term stability. However, while the generation of suitable frequency combs in the near-infrared is well established, extending these sources efficiently into the visible spectral range remains technically challenging. Here we propose a concept for a tunable visible frequency comb for the characterization and calibration of astronomical spectrographs. Near-infrared frequency comb lines are generated on a compact photonic chip driven by a continuous-wave laser, producing a comb centered at 1560 nm, which is subsequently down-converted to visible frequency combs centered at 520 nm and 390 nm, respectively. The individual comb lines can be swept over a wavelength range exceeding the native comb spacing, enabling characterization of the line spread function (LSF) of astronomical spectrographs across the frequency comb bandwidth.

Items.Authors: Dirk Schmidt
Items.Title: Blur: a fast simulation software for adaptive optics modeling and control systems testing
Items.Abstract: Blur is an adaptive optics (AO) software presenting third-party AO (realtime) control software (RTC) with simulated images of multiple wide-field Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensors (WFS).    It simulates turbulence and multiple deformable mirrors (DMs) including anisoplanatism in the subaperture images caused by turbulence and DMs far away from the pupil. Arbitrary extended or point objects can be used in the WFSs. Blur can also simulate the AO corrected “science image” of the scenery and compute wavefront errors within.    Blur is useful for AO performance modeling as well as for testing of AO RTC systems. It offers CoaXPress, CameraLink, Shared Memory and TCP interfaces for exchanging image and actuator data with the RTC. The RTC may run on the same or on a separate computer.     Blur is fast. It only takes 30 ms to simulate one update in the entire Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope multi-conjugate AO system (9 WFSs, 11817 subapertures, 3 DMs) on a 256-core AMD Epyc Zen 5 server.

Items.Authors: Kenta Yoneta, Jun Nishikawa, Yutaka Hayano, Masatsugu Iribe, Naoshi Murakami
Items.Title: Both-side dark hole generation technique based on Speckle Area Nulling (SAN)
Items.Abstract: Wavefront sensing and control (WFSC) is one of the key techniques for high-contrast imaging of exoplanets, suppressing scattered stellar light caused by wavefront aberrations to generate a dark hole. Speckle Area Nulling (SAN) method is the WFSC technique that does not require an optical propagation model in the high contrast imaging system. We have been developing the enhanced SAN method that can generate dark holes on both sides in the focal plane using two wavefront control devices, such as deformable mirrors. As a result of numerical simulations, the proposed method successfully generated both-side dark holes and achieved the stellar suppression performance equivalent to that of one-side dark hole generated by the conventional SAN method.

Items.Authors: Yulei Ding
Items.Title: Bright Dirac soliton microcomb in aluminum nitride microresonator
Items.Abstract: We demonstrate bright Dirac soliton generation in high Q AlN microresonators. By optimizing fabrication, we achieve record intrinsic Q factors exceeding 5.4 million at 1550 nm, with absorption Q factor over 8.0 million. To overcome the intrinsically normal dispersion of AlN waveguides, we harness spatial mode interactions between TE and TM modes to create broadband anomalous dispersion. Using a dual pump scheme, we generate stable Dirac soliton microcombs with 100 mW pump power and 113 GHz FSR—the lowest ever reported for AlN microcombs. The soliton spectrum agrees well with Dirac soliton theory. Polarization resolved measurements confirm its hybridized nature. This work enables bright soliton generation in normally dispersive crystalline platforms.

Items.Authors: Kuravi Hewawasam, Ananya Sahoo, Jasom Martel, Timothy A. Cook, Supriya Chakrabarti, Christopher B. Mendillo
Items.Title: Broadband electric field conjugation with a liquid crystal display-based spatial light modulator
Items.Abstract: Liquid crystal display (LCD) panels repurposed as phase-only spatial light modulators (SLMs) offer a low-cost alternative to deformable mirrors for focal plane wavefront control. Building on prior demonstrations of monochromatic speckle nulling, we present the implementation of broadband Electric Field Conjugation (EFC) using a transmissive LCD SLM integrated into a vector vortex coronagraph testbed operating over a finite spectral band. We present the EFC control model incorporating the coupled phase-amplitude behavior and chromatic retardance of the liquid crystal device. We demonstrate a broadband coronagraphic dark hole and quantify its contrast performance, stability, and convergence behavior. These results establish LCD-based SLMs as viable wavefront control elements for broadband high-contrast imaging and provide a scalable pathway for low-cost laboratory testbeds, technology development, and educational instrumentation.

Items.Authors: Saikrishna Manojkumar, Susan F. Redmond, Leonid Pogorelyuk, Christine L. Page, Garreth J. Ruane, Niyati Desai, Kerri L. Cahoy
Items.Title: Broadband focal plane modal estimation of high-order wavefront drifts on coronagraphic testbeds
Items.Abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) aims to directly image Exo-Earths 10 orders of magnitude dimmer than their host star. Algorithms such as dark zone maintenance (DZM) have been proposed to mitigate high-order wavefront drifts and maintain contrast. A modal dark zone maintenance (MDZM) approach, which represents and corrects drifting wavefronts in the deformable mirror (DM) actuator basis, has demonstrated improvement in closed-loop contrast performance by a factor of 5 in simulation in 2.5 in hardware. However, these results were confined to narrowband estimation and control. This work expands the MDZM formulation to use broadband images in simulation using the Decadal Survey Testbed (DST) simulator FALCO and in hardware using the In-Air Coronagraph Testbed (IACT) at NASA JPL. The resulting contrast performance is compared to traditional broadband DZM, as well as narrowband DZM and MDZM, across various drift rates and signal-to-noise ratios inside the dark zone of the speckles.
